column1: # models.tsv -- the simulated cohort, one row per model (SIMSET_CONTRACT v2, Doc 20)
# Columns are the contract's: model, components, proportions, generations,
# n_individuals, focal_ancestry, priority, cohort. components and proportions
# are comma lists in the same order, and proportions sum to 1.
# LAT3 IS 300, NOT THE CONTRACT TABLE'S 600.
# N_eff for the NAT component saturates: with 46 donors it is about 31.6 at
# n=200, 35.3 at 300 and 39.9 at 600. Going 200 -> 600 therefore spends 400
# extra imputation-server samples -- 19% of the whole cohort -- to buy roughly
# 8 effective genomes, because the ceiling is set by the DONOR pool, not by n.
# More donors raise the whole curve; more people do not.
# 300 keeps margin over 200 for any measure that wants raw count (switch-error
# rates are the candidate) while saving 14% of the server budget. Set it back
# to 600 here if the switch-error analysis turns out to need it -- nothing
# else has to change, because 6b batches from the donor lists and the cell
# deal rebalances itself.
# The AMR donor pool is the thing worth growing: the Peruvian Genome Project
# and the Indigenous American Genomic Diversity Project are both outstanding
# requests, and either would lift NAT N_eff at every n.
